A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AtomSurf, with matching core benchmarks, hybrid representation framework and scaling proposition. All pages, including appendices, equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original surface and hybrid-model experiments on PIP, MSP, PSR and MaSIF-ligand, architectural ablations, qualitative predictions and a PSR learning-curve comparison.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds evaluations of another model configuration, RNA segmentation, antibody–antigen binding-site detection, and computational and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: Beyond naming the original benchmark hybrid AtomSurf-bench, v3 introduces a distinct AtomSurf variant using residue graphs, pretrained ESM features, ProNet graph encoding and GVP messages between representations. Reported bipartite connectivity changes from an 8-angstrom cutoff to 16 nearest neighbors, and dynamic batching is introduced. These are procedural additions and revisions, not merely expanded descriptions.

E1.justification: The three protein-only Atom3D tasks and MaSIF-ligand are retained. v3 additionally evaluates functional segmentation of 5S ribosomal RNA surfaces and antibody–antigen binding-site detection. These introduce a new molecular domain and distinct residue-level prediction requirements.

E2.justification: v3 Table 2 adds ProNet, GVP, GVP-ESM and GearNet-ESM comparisons on retained Atom3D tasks, and Table 3 adds ProNet to MaSIF-ligand. New evaluations compare against DGCNN, DeltaConv and GEP. The parallel fusion comparator disappears from the architectural ablation; HoloProt is the renamed v2 holo comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds a richer 600k-parameter evaluation setting alongside the restricted benchmark model, plus antibody–antigen evaluation with a 186/49 train/test split, antibody scoring restricted to CDRs, and MCC reporting. Reported minimum mesh size changes from 128 to 256 vertices, and diffusion initialization changes from N(2,2) to N(10,5). Original dataset splits are retained in Appendix E. For MaSIF-ligand, the prose still specifies balanced accuracy while Table 3 says AuROC, so an actual metric switch cannot be established.

E4.justification: v3 adds RNA training-stability comparisons, diffusion-scale visualizations, learned-time distributions, memory profiling and distance-threshold sensitivity including out-of-memory failures. The existing PSR stabilization analysis is retained and supplemented with a results table. Qualitative protein examples are replaced, while the parallel-fusion and separate depth comparisons in v2 Table 3 are removed from v3 Table 4.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seed counts, replicated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. v3's approximately 100 model trainings describe aggregate computational expenditure across settings and failed experiments, not repeated-run statistical estimation.

E6.justification: The original hybrid benchmark scores are retained as AtomSurf-bench. New AtomSurf results include PIP 0.907, MSP 0.715 and PSR local/global correlations 0.613/0.861 under the richer configuration, rather than demonstrating same-setting gains over v2. New results include RNA accuracy of 84.1% versus original DiffusionNet's 80.9%, and antibody MCC of 0.47 versus GEP's 0.28. Additional baseline, sensitivity and computational results appear, while ablation entries are revised or removed.

T1.justification: The Brownian-motion scaling proposition and its proof are retained with renumbering. v3 corrects an eigenfunction index in the initial heat-kernel formula, although inconsistent indices remain later in the derivation. Appendix D.1 adds an auxiliary asymptotic runtime analysis of diffusion, graph encoding and bipartite message passing.

C1.justification: v3 retains the central claim that integrating graph and surface representations improves protein learning, but expands the claimed contributions to antibody–antigen binding-site detection, richer sequence-informed representations and competitive computational throughput. Its conclusion claims state-of-the-art results across several benchmark tasks, whereas v2 claimed them across all benchmark tasks.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive explanations of computational applicability: coarsening shifts the runtime bottleneck toward graph encoding, while variable mesh sizes cause memory spikes and restrict batching. It also attributes stronger competing PSR performance to explicit geometric priors and revises the explanation of sequential fusion's weakness from optimization difficulty toward inadequate simultaneous multiscale communication. The high-memory limitation remains.

D1.justification: v3 documents additional feature construction, mesh cleaning, neighborhood construction, a 0.1 coarsening rate and dynamic batching. Appendix D.3 newly reports hardware, training durations and aggregate training expenditure. The stated repository changes from atom2D to atomsurf, and pip-package availability is mentioned. Existing block widths and depths mostly move from Appendix A to Appendix C rather than becoming newly disclosed settings.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around multimodal protein learning, discussing Lee et al., Pegoraro et al. and Xu et al. and contrasting their fusion or pretraining approaches with communication across intermediate layers. It also incorporates protein-language-model integration and newer geometric encoders. This extends the scientific comparison beyond v2's narrower treatment of surface methods and HoloProt.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introductory and methodological passages are rewritten. v3 introduces a dedicated Motivation and Contribution section, reorganizes the method presentation, distinguishes Surface Diff, AtomSurf-bench and AtomSurf, and moves detailed dataset descriptions and architectural alternatives into expanded appendices. These changes substantially reshape the narrative.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text from two columns to one, redraws the architecture diagrams, consolidates and transposes the original benchmark tables, and replaces the ligand-classification bar chart with a table. It also replaces the qualitative prediction panels and adds binding-detection, diffusion-scale, memory and supplementary-result displays. These are substantial visual changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens v2's limited validation through contemporary competing methods, independent RNA and antibody–antigen tasks, and targeted diffusion, threshold and memory analyses. Separating restricted benchmarking from the richer model also makes the comparisons more informative, while computational disclosures improve practical assessability. These gains outweigh the loss of depth and parallel-fusion ablations and new reporting inconsistencies, notably Table 3's AuROC label despite balanced-accuracy prose and inconsistent model naming in the binding-detection discussion.
